chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā narrated from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from Abī Ayyūb, from Ismāʿīl ibn Jābir, who said:

I said to Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: I am occupied. He said, “Then do as we do: perform six rakʿahs when the sun is in a position like its position at the ʿasr prayer, meaning the higher rise of the forenoon, and count them as from zawāl.”

key_terms.الشَّمْسُ: the sun, used here to indicate prayer timing
key_terms.صَلَاةَ الْعَصْرِ: the ʿasr prayer, used as a positional time reference

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام instruct an occupied person to do regarding six rakʿahs before noon?
ai.summary: This hadith reports a legal instruction from Imam Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام regarding performing six rakʿahs at a specified time of day for one who is occupied. It indicates a ruling connected to the reckoning of these prayers from the time of zawāl and relates to the scheduling of recommended salat.
